title: No Es Que… Sino Que…: Correcting a Reason About Medellín

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *no es que* + subjunctive, *sino que* + indicative from B2 Unit 5: you reject a reason people might assume and give the real one. Medellín's story is full of assumptions to correct, about its climate, its past and its change. The first part is a reason you say is not true, so it takes the subjunctive; the second part is the real reason, in the indicative.

sections.title: Reject one reason, give the real one
rows: No es que haga mucho calor, sino que la temperatura casi no cambia.
No es que los problemas hayan desaparecido, sino que la ciudad ha cambiado mucho.
No es que Medellín sea fría, sino que su clima es templado.

items.spanish: No es que Medellín tenga mucho calor, sino que su clima es templado todo el año.
items.english: It is not that Medellín is very hot, but that its climate is mild all year.

items.spanish: No es que la violencia haya terminado, sino que, según las cifras oficiales, ha bajado desde 1991.
items.english: It is not that violence has ended, but that, according to official figures, it has fallen since 1991.

items.spanish: No es que el Metrocable sea solo un transporte, sino que conecta barrios con el metro.
items.english: It is not that the Metrocable is only a means of transport, but that it connects districts with the metro.

items.spanish: No era que la ciudad no tuviera problemas, sino que ya no era la de los años noventa.
items.english: It was not that the city had no problems, but that it was no longer the city of the 1990s.

sections.content: Use this pattern when you expect someone to draw a wrong conclusion. It corrects a reason, not a person. *Sino que* always keeps its *que* and takes the indicative. On a painful topic, attribute the judgement (*según las cifras oficiales*, *según los críticos*) instead of stating it as your own.
